values: detekt
catch-log-without-exception
A scan of the Kotlin sources on the Node side reports it under the tool detekt.
A `catch` block that logs a failure without passing the caught exception to the logger.

Pass the caught exception to the logger as its own argument so the stack trace is kept (log.error("what failed", e), or logger.error(e) { "what failed" }). e.message, e.toString() and a string template of the exception drop it.
inline-suppression
A `@Suppress` would hide a finding from the report, so a source scan reports every token that targets one.
An inline `@Suppress` of a detekt or ktlint rule, a ruleset, `all` or a compiler warning the kotlinc lint reports.

values.note: No exception applies: the routes are to fix the code, and `exclude` for generated code.

values: test-without-assertion
A test method that calls no assertion.

Assert the result (assertEquals, assertFailsWith, `shouldBe`, MockK `verify`): this test has no assertion, so it passes whenever the code does not throw. A project helper that asserts is learned from the tests that end with it (conventions kotlin.assertionHelpers).
kotlin-source
BooleanFlagParameter

A scan of the Kotlin sources on the Node side, after comments and string bodies are masked, reports it: the Kotlin counterpart of a TypeScript, Java or Python rule that narrows one spot to one allowed form.

An unannotated `Boolean` parameter (not a nullable `Boolean?`) of a public function that is the condition of an `if`, a `when` (its subject or a branch of a subject-less one) or a `while`, also as `== true` or in `&&`/`||`, and a name the body rebinds (a loop variable, a lambda parameter, a `val`) is not the flag; private, `internal`, `protected` and `override` functions, functions of a private or `internal` class, local functions, setters, `with*`, `of`/`from`/`valueOf`/`builder` are skipped.

Split the function into two functions named for each behavior, or pass an enum or a small data class: this boolean parameter switches the function between two behaviors, which makes the call site unreadable.
CatchOnlyLogsOrReturnsDefault

A `catch` that neither throws, nor uses the exception, nor answers with an error response; log calls and `printStackTrace` do not count (so it is the one finding for a catch that only logs); an interrupt and a retry loop are skipped.

Rethrow it with the cause (`throw OrderException(message, e)`), return a failure result that carries the exception (`Result.failure(e)`), or answer with an error response: this catch only logs the failure or returns a default, and carries on.
CommentedOutCode
A run of line comments, or a block comment, whose first code-shaped line is a declaration, call, assignment, control header, `fun`, `class`, import or return.
Delete the commented-out code; version control keeps it.
CredentialLiteral
An AWS key, a GitHub or Slack token, a `sk_live_`/`sk-proj-` key, a private key header, a password in a URL or a `Bearer`/`Basic` value.
Read it from the environment or a secrets manager: this string looks like a credential (access key, token, private key, or a password in a URL).
DetachedTestCase

(test sources) a public no-argument function with a block body and no return type (or `: Unit`) named like a test (backticks, `test*`, `should*`) without an annotation, in a class that has tests; a helper or data provider that returns a value passes.
Annotate the function with @Test so JUnit runs it, or make it private if it is a helper: this test never runs.
GeneratedOnHandWrittenCode

An annotation named `Generated` (any package, also `@get:`/`@set:`) on a class, object, interface, function or constructor (JaCoCo and PIT skip it), as the Java rule; `@GeneratedValue` and `@Generated` on a property pass.
Remove the annotation from hand-written code: JaCoCo and PIT skip a class, function or constructor annotated @Generated, so this is not measured.
GenericPackageName
A package segment `util`, `utils`, `utility`, `helpers`, `manager`, `common`, `commons`, `misc`.
Name this package for what it holds, not utils, helpers, common or misc. Pure logic shared between features goes in the shared package under a name that says what it does.
GenericTypeName
A class, interface or object named `*Util(s)`, `*Utility`, `*Utilities`, `*Helper`, `*Manager`, `*Common(s)`, `*Misc`; framework roles and a type that extends one with the same ending are skipped.
Name this type for what it does (`PriceRounder`, `OrderTotals`), not Utils, Helper, Manager, Common or Misc. Pure logic shared between features goes in the shared package under such a name.
HardcodedSecret
A secret-looking literal assigned to a name like `*password`, `*secret`, `*token`, `*apiKey`, also as a named argument, a `"key" to "value"` pair or a `"key", "value"` argument pair.
Read it from the environment or a secrets manager and inject it: this variable holds a hardcoded secret.
HttpWithoutTimeout

A `java.net.http` request built without `.timeout(...)`, an `HttpURLConnection` from an HTTP URL whose block never sets `readTimeout`, `URL(...).readText()`/`readBytes()`/`openStream()`, `RestTemplate()`, `HttpClients.createDefault()`; OkHttp and Ktor pass (their engines set timeouts).

Give the call a deadline: `HttpRequest.newBuilder(uri).timeout(Duration.ofSeconds(10))` (java.net.http), `connectTimeout` and `readTimeout` on an `HttpURLConnection`, a client with timeouts (OkHttp, which sets them by default, or Ktor with `install(HttpTimeout) { requestTimeoutMillis = 10_000 }`), `RestTemplateBuilder().connectTimeout(...).readTimeout(...)` for Spring, or `RequestConfig.custom().setResponseTimeout(...)` for the Apache client. This HTTP call has no timeout, so a server that never answers hangs it for good.
IoCallInLoop

A repository, DAO, JDBC or HTTP client call in a `for`, `while` or `do` body or an iterating lambda (`forEach`, `map`, `filter` and similar); paging and polling loops (a `while` or `do` whose condition, `if (...) break` or `?: break` reads what the call returned) and retries (the call in a `try` that leaves the loop) pass; file calls are not checked.

Fetch or write all items at once (`findAllById`, `saveAll`, `deleteAll`, `WHERE id IN (...)`, one batched request): this calls a database, HTTP or repository API once per loop item. Paging, polling and retry loops are fine.
LogStringConcatenation

An `info`, `warn`, `error`, `log`, `config`, `warning` or `severe` call on a logger (the levels of the Java rule) whose message is a string template, `+` or `format` with a value that is not a compile-time constant (a literal, a `CONSTANT_CASE` name or a `const val` is one).
Pass values as placeholders (`log.info("user {}", user)`), or give a lambda logger the message (`logger.info { "user $user" }`), not a message built with a string template, `+` or `format`.
MutableModuleState
A top-level `var`, or a mutable collection, array, atomic or `MutableStateFlow` in a top-level `val`, or either in an `object` or companion object.

Keep state in an instance: a class whose object the composition root creates and passes in, holding `val`s and immutable `listOf`/`mapOf`. A top-level `var` or a mutable collection in an `object` is shared by the whole program.
MutationIgnoreMarker
`@DoNotMutate`, `@CoverageIgnore`.
Remove the annotation and kill the mutants with a test: PIT does not mutate code annotated @DoNotMutate or @CoverageIgnore.
RepeatedStringLiteral

A string of 5 or more characters (with a letter or digit, no `$` template) used three times in a main source file; every use from the third on is reported. A `const val` initializer counts as a use. Not counted: annotation arguments, `when (subject)` branch labels, named arguments (`label = "..."`), map and `to` pair keys, `x["key"]` subscripts, the value of a `"type"`/`"kind"`/`"tag"`/`"variant"` pair, the first argument of a translation or message-key call (`t`, `translate`, `formatMessage`, `getMessage`, `getString`, `gettext` and the like) and idiomatic text (encodings, HTTP methods, MIME types, time formats, argparse actions). Test sources are not scanned.
A string is repeated three times or more in the file. Name it once as a constant (`private const val NAME = "..."`) and use the constant.
SecretInLog
A secret-named value passed to a log call (any level, Android `Log.d` too) or `print`, directly, in a `+`, in a template or in a lambda message (`logger.info { "token $token" }`).
Log that the secret is set, or a masked tail, instead of the secret itself.
ShellCommand
A shell and its command flag as consecutive literals (`"sh", "-c"`, `"bash", "-c"`, `"cmd", "/c"`, `"powershell", "-Command"`).
Run the program directly with an argument list (`ProcessBuilder("git", "log", ref)`), not through a shell with `-c`.
SqlStringBuilding

SQL text built from a runtime value with a string template, `+`, `String.format` or `.format`: text that starts like a statement or clause in capitals (`SELECT ... FROM`, `UPDATE ... SET`, `AND name =`), or any case when it reaches a JDBC, Spring `JdbcTemplate`, JPA or R2DBC query call directly or through a `val`.

Pass values as bind parameters: `jdbcTemplate.query("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?", mapper, id)`, `prepareStatement("... WHERE id = ?")` with `setLong(1, id)`, `:id` with `NamedParameterJdbcTemplate` or JPA `setParameter("id", id)`, or a query DSL (Exposed, jOOQ). Build placeholder lists from placeholders alone (`ids.joinToString(", ") { "?" }`), optional filters from literal fragments joined with `" AND "`, and take a table or column name from a constant or an enum. This SQL text is built from a runtime value with a string template, `+` or `format`, so the value can change the statement (SQL injection).
TestClassWithoutTestCases

(test sources) a class named `*Test`, `*Tests`, `*TestCase` or `*IT` with no test annotation in it; abstract and open classes, Kotest specs and classes with a superclass, suites and `@Nested` are skipped.
Add @Test functions to the class, or rename it if it is a helper (for example `TestInputGenerator` becomes `InputGenerator`): a test class without tests never runs.
TestHelperInSource
A main source that imports JUnit, kotlin.test, Kotest, MockK, Mockito, AssertJ, Truth, Strikt or Hamcrest.
Move the test helper to the test sources (`src/test/kotlin`): production code must not import a test framework.
TlsVerificationOff

An empty `checkServerTrusted`, a host-name verifier or trust strategy that returns `true`, `NoopHostnameVerifier`, `TrustAllStrategy`, `TrustSelfSignedStrategy`, Netty's `InsecureTrustManagerFactory` (its use, not its import).

Keep certificate and host-name verification on and trust the certificate authority instead: load it into a `KeyStore` and build the `SSLContext` from `TrustManagerFactory.getInstance(TrustManagerFactory.getDefaultAlgorithm()).apply { init(keyStore) }`, use OkHttp `HandshakeCertificates.Builder().addTrustedCertificate(certificate)`, or set `-Djavax.net.ssl.trustStore` for a private CA. This trusts any certificate or host name, so anyone on the network can pose as the server, and turning it off by environment ships the switch to production.
UnsafeDeserialization

`XMLDecoder`, Jackson `enableDefaultTyping`, `activateDefaultTyping` with `LaissezFaireSubTypeValidator`, `JsonTypeInfo.Id.CLASS`/`MINIMAL_CLASS`, `SerializationUtils.deserialize`, Kryo without class registration (`ObjectInputStream` is detekt's `ForbiddenMethodCall`).

Read the data as JSON into a concrete type: `Json.decodeFromString<Order>(text)` with kotlinx.serialization or `mapper.readValue<Order>(text)` with Jackson, with polymorphism by a logical name (a `sealed` class with kotlinx.serialization, or `@JsonTypeInfo(use = JsonTypeInfo.Id.NAME)` with `@JsonSubTypes`). This reads class names or objects from the data, so a crafted payload builds any class on the classpath and runs code.
WeakHash

`MessageDigest`, `Signature`, `DigestUtils` with MD2, MD4, MD5 or SHA-1 (a literal, a constant in the file or a commons-codec constant), commons-codec, Spring, Guava and Okio MD5/SHA-1 helpers, and HMAC-MD5 (`Mac`, `KeyGenerator`, `HmacUtils`, its own message); HMAC-SHA1 passes.

Hash with `MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-256")` (or SHA-384, SHA-512, SHA3-256), sign with `Mac.getInstance("HmacSHA256")`, and hash passwords with Argon2 or bcrypt (`Argon2PasswordEncoder`, `BCryptPasswordEncoder`): MD5 and SHA-1 are broken hashes, collisions are cheap and brute force is fast. A protocol you do not control that requires one (a legacy signature, an ETag, a WebSocket accept key) is the exception.
kotlinc
cast
The kotlinc lint compiles the main Kotlin sources with the pinned compiler and reports these warnings as findings, like -Werror on the code the change touched; a build setting cannot hide them.
A Kotlin compiler warning: `USELESS_CAST`.
Remove the cast.
deprecation
A Kotlin compiler warning: `DEPRECATION`, `TYPEALIAS_EXPANSION_DEPRECATION`.
Call the replacement the deprecation names (its `ReplaceWith`, or the Javadoc of a Java API).
lint-not-run
Without the lint compile, the compiler warnings above are not checked, so the run says so.
The kotlinc lint could not compile the sources, for example because a compiler plugin could not be loaded.

No kotlinc lint report from the lint compile (kotlinc exited with an error), so unchecked casts, deprecated calls and redundant casts were not checked. Fix what that compile reports (the main sources, the compile class path and the compiler plugins).

pmd
AssertionInControlFlow
One of the review rules of the Kotlin preset, a scan of the Kotlin sources on the Node side; it prints as a PMD rule, like the Java rules it mirrors.
An assertion that can be skipped: inside an `if` or a `when` whose branches do not all assert, a loop, a safe call, `&&`, `||`, `?:`, a swallowing `try` or `runCatching`, or after an early return.

Assert unconditionally. An assertion inside an if, a when, a loop, a safe call, a try/catch that swallows the failure or a runCatching can be skipped, so the test passes without checking anything: a loop over an empty list, or a branch the data never takes, checks nothing. Assert in every branch (an if/else or when whose branches all assert or fail is fine), or narrow with assertNotNull, assertIs or `?: fail(...)` instead of an if or a safe call. Put a table of cases in a parameterized test (@ParameterizedTest with @MethodSource or @CsvSource, Kotest withData) and assert every time; for a loop over results, assert the whole collection at once (assertEquals(expected, results), shouldContainExactly, AssertJ containsExactly). Do not return early before the assertions, and let assertion errors escape. An exception fits only a case that cannot be stated unconditionally, such as cases generated at run time.
CoroutineEscapesTest
A `launch`, `async`, `launchIn`, `stateIn` or `shareIn` on a scope the test does not own (`CoroutineScope(...)`, a scope field, `viewModelScope`) that nothing joins, awaits or cancels.

This test starts a coroutine that the test does not wait for, so it can still be running, or fail, after the test has passed: a launch, async, launchIn, stateIn or shareIn on CoroutineScope(...), MainScope(), a scope kept in a field or a local, a scope a helper returns, lifecycleScope or viewModelScope without a test Main dispatcher, or a TestScope outside runTest is not a child of the test, and with, run, apply or also on such a scope does not change that. Run the body in runTest (or runBlocking, coroutineScope, supervisorScope) and launch from there, keep the Job or Deferred and join or await it (`val job = scope.launch { ... }; job.join()`), or build the scope on the test dispatcher and drive it with advanceUntilIdle; `backgroundScope.launch` inside runTest is for work that should end with the test. An exception fits only when the test waits through a harness this rule cannot see.
DisabledTest

A skipped test: `@Disabled`, `@Ignore`, `@Ignored` (also aliased or carried by an annotation), Kotest `xtest`, `xcontext`, `xdescribe`, `xit`, `xshould`, `xgiven`, a `!` name prefix, a `.config(...)` that never runs, a constant false condition or assumption.

Fix or delete this test instead of disabling it: @Disabled, @Ignore, @Ignored (also through an alias or an annotation that carries them), an x-prefixed Kotest name (xtest, xcontext, xdescribe, xit, xshould, xgiven), a "!" name prefix, `.config(enabled = false)`, a condition that is always false and an assumption that is always false all skip it while the build stays green, so nothing shows that the behavior it covered is unchecked. Delete the test when the behavior is gone; to run it only where it can run, use a condition on the environment (`@EnabledOnOs`, `@EnabledIfSystemProperty`, an assumption on a real condition). An exception fits only a test that is skipped on purpose until a tracked defect is fixed.
FocusedTest
A Kotest focus that runs only part of the suite: the `f:` name prefix, `ftest`, `fcontext`, `fdescribe`, `fit`, `fshould`, `fgiven`.

Remove the focus from this test: a Kotest name with the "f:" prefix and the f-prefixed registrations (ftest, fcontext, fdescribe, fit, fshould, fgiven) make Kotest run only the focused tests of the spec, so the rest of the suite is skipped while the build stays green. Run one test while you work with the IDE or a Gradle `--tests` filter, and commit the test without the focus.
